title: Detection of possible glycine precursor molecule methylamine towards the hot molecular core G358.93─0.03 MM1
question: Is the possible glycine precursor methylamine detectable in the hot molecular core G358.93–0.03 MM1 with ALMA band 7, what are its LTE column density, excitation temperature and abundance, and what does its abundance say about its formation route? Glycine itself was also searched for.

data.angular_resolution: 0.42 arcsec (table); synthesized beams 0.425x0.369, 0.427x0.376, 0.413x0.364, 0.410x0.358 arcsec per window

what.value: Column density of the abundance-reference species (name lost in text) towards MM1, (1.25±0.11)×10^24 cm^-2, used as denominator for the fractional abundance
Column density of the second molecule (name lost in text) towards MM1, (5.9±2.5)×10^14 cm^-2, used for the column density ratio
Column density of the abundance-reference species towards MM3, (3.51±0.7)×10^23 cm^-2, used for the MM3 upper limit abundance
Systemic velocities V_LSR of MM1 (–16.5 km/s) and MM3 (–18.2 km/s)

evidence.quote: are –16.5 km s$^{-1}$ and –18.2 km s$^{-1}$, respectively (cite: bro19)

what.value: Distance 6.75 (+0.37/-0.68) kpc, luminosity ~7.7e3 Lsun and total gas mass 167±12 Msun of G358.93–0.03

evidence.quote: The luminosity of G358.93–0.03 is $\sim$7.7$\times$10$^{3}$ L$_{\odot}$ and the total gas mass is 167$\pm$12M$_{\odot}$ (cite: bro19).

what.value: Gas density of the warm inner hot core, 2×10^7 cm^-3, used to justify LTE

evidence.quote: because the gas density of the warm inner region of the hot core was 2$\times$10$^{7}$ cm$^{-3}$ (cite: ste21)

what.value: Perley-Butler 2017 flux calibrator model used for flux scale

evidence.quote: We used the Perley-Butler 2017 flux calibrator model for flux calibration with flux calibrator J1550+0527 for each baseline using the task `SETJY` (cite: pal17).

recipe.goal: calibrate and image the band 7 data
recipe.method: ALMA pipeline calibration in CASA (flux with setjy, bandpass and flag tasks), split target with mstransform, continuum image with tclean, continuum subtraction with uvcontsub, spectral cubes with tclean (Briggs robust 0.5), primary-beam correction with impbcor

recipe.goal: extract spectra from MM1 and MM3
recipe.method: Spectra from a 0.91 arcsec diameter circular region around each hot core
key_parameters: 0.91 arcsec diameter circular region, larger than the line emitting regions

recipe.goal: identify methylamine lines and fit LTE model
recipe.method: LTE-RADEX module in CASSIS with JPL spectroscopy; ~250 other molecules fitted too to handle blending; best-fit column density, excitation temperature and source size
key_parameters: Best fit: N = (1.10±0.31)e17 cm^-2, Tex = 180.8±25.5 K, source size 0.5 arcsec
assumptions: LTE valid because the inner hot core gas density is 2e7 cm^-3

recipe.goal: check temperature with a rotational diagram
recipe.method: Gaussian fits to the five non-blended lines in the CASSIS line analysis module, then a straight-line fit of ln(Nu/gu) against Eu
key_parameters: Partition function 15560 at 75 K, 44047 at 150 K, 124715 at 300 K

recipe.goal: derive fractional abundance and column density ratio
recipe.method: Column density within the 0.45 arcsec beam divided by the reference column density from the earlier paper; column density ratio to a second molecule
key_parameters: Reference column density (1.25±0.11)e24 cm^-2 and second-molecule column density (5.9±2.5)e14 cm^-2, both from (cite: man23a)

recipe.goal: map the emission and estimate emitting regions
recipe.method: Integrated emission maps of the five non-blended lines with immoments, overlaid on the 1.02 mm continuum; 2D Gaussian fits with imfit; deconvolved size from theta_S = sqrt(theta_50^2 - theta_beam^2)
key_parameters: theta_50 is the diameter of the circle enclosing the 50% line peak area; theta_beam is the half-power beam width

recipe.goal: derive upper limits for MM3 and glycine
recipe.method: LTE-modelled spectra compared with the data; 3 sigma upper limit column densities

recipe.goal: compare with warm-up chemical models and other sources
recipe.method: Observed fractional abundance compared with fast, medium and slow warm-up model abundances of Garrod (2013) and with literature abundances in G10.47+0.03, Sgr B2, Orion KL
assumptions: Model is applicable because MM1 temperature is ~150 K and gas density ~2e7 cm^-3
